rv.q: Written while Wilde was serving the last stretch of his sentence in Reading Gaol between January and March 1897, it’s a 50,000-word letter addressed to his estranged lover, Lord Alfred “Bosie” Douglas. It’s a gorgeous, touching reclaiming of the narrative he was crucified for, with Wilde transforming his personal tragedy into art.

Here, the actor is Jens Harzer, who inhabits the desperate side of Wilde, the one who loved too deeply and lived too much for pleasure. In Reese’s vision of the piece, Harzer offers a deeply physical and often unsettling depiction of a man trapped in body and soul.
For last year the most famous German theatre company, the Berliner Ensemble, produced the letter as a play in its Berlin home, and now brings it to London for a short run.

With nowhere to go and reams of monologue to deliver, he keeps constantly active in jittery, repetitive physicality that underscores Wilde’s fragility, yet with fiercely emotional and moving speech. Through the early part of the letter, Wilde is a shining, ethereal visage as he describes the impact of the toxic relationship.
